subject.title: Feature: Silence Watchdog + Response Delivery Confirmation — runtime-enforced operator visibility

question: Should this issue remain the umbrella for a default runtime silence watchdog plus cross-channel response-delivery confirmation contract, or should maintainers split it into narrower canonical delivery and watchdog issues?
rationale: The remaining work chooses channel-agnostic defaults, new config shape, retry/alert semantics, no-response policy, and ownership boundaries, which are broader than a safe autonomous bug fix.

options.title: Keep Umbrella Open
options.body: Use this issue as the cross-channel product umbrella while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77771, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46830, and Telegram-specific PRs land as implementation slices.

options.title: Split And Close Later
options.body: Designate separate canonical issues for silence watchdogs and response-delivery confirmation, then close this issue only after those links preserve the combined context.

options.title: Narrow To Delivery Only
options.body: Retitle or scope this issue to end-of-turn delivery confirmation and leave silence-watchdog work to the existing task-watchdog issue or a new maintainer-owned issue.

recommendation.title: Keep Umbrella Open
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the cross-channel product umbrella while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/87561, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/77771, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46830, and Telegram-specific PRs land as implementation slices.

likelyOwner.reason: The open durable final fallback delivery semantics issue is the hardest product-contract half of this umbrella, making its author the best current routing candidate for the maintainer choice.
